lines.t: Hello! Welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
Hi! I'm Sam. Today we talk about food and cooking.
Sam, can you cook?
Yes! Yesterday I cooked rice in my kitchen. I'm hungry now!
Was it good?
It smells good. But the rice is a little hot, and a little black.
Black? Sam!
It is OK. I have bread and an egg. I can cut up the egg. Can I help?
Wash up first. Wash your hands. And sit down. Tell me everything.
I put the rice in the pan. I went to the other room. I came back. It was black.
You went to the other room?
Yes. I looked at my phone for five minutes.
That is your recipe, your cooking plan. Phone, five minutes, black rice.
I'm hungry. Let us have bread. Bye for now!
[laugh] Bye!

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is cooking at home. And last night I cooked dinner for Tom.
Tom, your flatmate with the plant?
Yes, Karen's owner. I found a recipe online. It said, "Easy pilaf. Thirty minutes."
How did it turn out?
First, I boiled the rice. Then I fried the onions. Then I forgot the salt.
Oh, Sam.
Tom tasted it and said, "It needs more salt." I put in more salt. A lot. He said, "Tasty! It's delicious!" Then he drank two litres of water.
[laugh] Don't mix up the salt and the sugar.
I know. But the ingredients were the same colour. I said, "Sit down, dinner is ready." And Tom said, "Thank you, my friend. I will eat up." He ate up everything. Slowly.
You are a good friend.
Now he heats up bread in the toaster and says he is on a diet.
Can you pass the salt? My dad was a baker, and he said, "Cooking is love and salt."
Then my pilaf was full of love. See you next time!

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is cooking, and my disaster pilaf.
Let's hear the full story. Did you make it from scratch?
Yes. Fresh onions, fresh carrots, homemade stock. I chopped everything. Then I put the rice in the pot and let it simmer.
And then?
And then Tom called. His ex called him. He cried for twenty minutes. And the pilaf burnt.
[laugh] Burnt pilaf.
I tried to save it. I stirred in some water, filled up the pot, and added seasoning. It turned out like soup. Spicy soup. Very spicy.
There are too many cooks in your flat.
Two cooks, one pot and a breakup. I had a lot on my plate.
So what happened to the leftovers?
Tom ate them for three days. He said it made him forget his ex.
Maybe you should open a restaurant for broken hearts.
Great idea. The menu: one dish. Question for our listeners: what is the worst thing you ever cooked?
Mine was a cake. It came out like a hat. See you next time!
